subtype: Approach: asks a trusted adult a direct question [Action]
passage:
Ojas sat on the shop step in the small town with one school shoe on and the other's laces hanging loose. He tried, twisted, and the laces slid apart. He sighed. "Dada, will you show me how to tie it?"

Dada put down the newspaper. "Watch slowly, beta. Cross. Tuck. Make a bunny ear."

Ojas watched, chin on his knees. Then Dada put his big hands over Ojas's small ones, and together they pulled the loops tight. "Now you."

Ojas stuck out his tongue and crossed the laces alone. The bow was lopsided, but it held. "I did it!"

qa.q: What did Dada say to do?
qa.a: Dada said to cross, tuck and make a bunny ear.

qa.q: How did Ojas feel after tying the bow?
qa.a: Ojas felt proud and happy, and called out "I did it!"

qa.q: What could Ojas do to get better at tying the bow?
qa.a: Ojas could practise a little each day with Dada nearby, and ask to be shown slowly again if he gets stuck.

qa.q: How might Dada feel while showing Ojas?
qa.a: Dada might feel patient and pleased to see Ojas learn.

grounding: Shows a child asking his grandfather to show him how to tie laces and trying with the grandfather's hands guiding his.

subtype: Approach: asks a trusted adult a direct question [Action]
passage: Xin's new trainers had real laces, like the ones his friend Yosef tied all by himself. At the door, Xin tugged the loops into a knot that fell apart twice. He sat on the step, then looked up. "Yeye, can you show me? Slowly?" Grandpa knelt down. "Watch. Bunny ear, then round the tree, then through the hole." He did it once, very slowly. Then he put his big warm hands over Xin's small ones and they made the bunny ear together. The first bow was lopsided. The second one held all the way to the park.

qa.q: Why did Xin want to learn to tie his laces?
qa.a: He wanted to be like his friend Yosef, and he felt frustrated when his knot kept falling apart; he hoped Yeye's help would fix it.

qa.q: What small step helped Xin most?
qa.a: Grandpa's hands guiding his made the steps easy to feel; next time Xin could try alone while Grandpa just watches.

qa.q: How might Yeye feel being asked for help?
qa.a: Yeye probably felt pleased and patient, glad that Xin trusted him enough to ask.

grounding: A child who cannot tie laces asks his grandfather to show him, watches slowly, then ties with the grandfather's hands guiding his.

subtype: Approach: asks a trusted adult a direct question [Action]
passage: After swimming class at the sports club, Ojas pulled on his school shoes and stared at the flapping laces. Tejas, from his class, was already out of the door. Ojas carried his shoe to the bench where Dadu waited. "Dadu, teach me the loops. Tejas can do it." Dadu set the shoe on his knee. "Look carefully." He made one loop, wrapped the other lace round it and pulled, very slowly. "Now you." It flopped open. Dadu covered Ojas's fingers with his own. "Together." Round, through, pull. Ojas grinned at the bow.

qa.a: On the bench, where Ojas carried his shoe after swimming class.

qa.q: What might Ojas be feeling when Tejas was already out of the door?
qa.a: He probably felt a little left behind and embarrassed that he couldn't tie his laces yet, which pushed him to ask Dadu.

qa.q: What would you advise Ojas's teacher at the club if other children need the same help?
qa.a: Show the loops slowly once, then guide each child's hands, the same way Dadu did, before letting them try alone.

qa.q: How does Dadu see Ojas's request?
qa.a: Dadu seems happy to be asked and takes it seriously, slowing down so Ojas can actually learn.

grounding: A young child asks his grandfather a direct question about laces, watches, then practises with the grandfather's hands guiding.
